# Unique usernames

Implement `Registry` in `solution.py`, keeping all state in `runtime.Store` (see
`runtime.py`). Each user holds at most one name, and each name belongs to at most one
user.

```python
Registry(store)
register(user: str, name: str) -> bool
rename(user: str, new_name: str) -> bool
owner(name: str) -> str | None
name_of(user: str) -> str | None
```

- Names are 1 to 16 characters from `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, compared case-insensitively:
  `Bob` and `bob` are the same name. Store and return names in lower case. Calls with
  an invalid name return `False` (or `None` for `owner`) and change nothing.
- `register` gives `user` the name if the user has no name and nobody holds the name.
  Registering the name the user already holds returns `True`. Otherwise `False`.
- `rename` moves a user who holds a name to `new_name` if nobody else holds it; the
  old name becomes free. Renaming to the name the user already holds returns `True`.
  On `False`, nothing changes.
- `owner` and `name_of` return the current holder and name.
- Many `Registry` objects in many threads may share one `Store`. Calls for the same
  user never overlap; calls for different users may. When no call is in progress,
  `owner(n) == u` exactly when `name_of(u) == n`.

Use P to model the design before implementing it, and to test the implementation.
`snappea` and the `pysnappea` Python package are installed. Keep your P files and
tests in this directory; the tests must run with `python -m pytest`.
----
---
name: p-modeling
description: Design concurrent or retrying code with a P model checked by snappea, then test the real implementation against what the model found.
---

# P modeling

P finds bugs that only appear in some orderings: two clients read the same version,
a retry arrives after the state changed, a step fails between read and write. Use it
for shared state, retries, concurrency and recovery. Pure transformations need only
ordinary tests.

The model is worth what it changes in the code and tests. Follow these steps in order.

## 1. List the risks (before any code)

Write down, in `DESIGN.md`:

- the contract in checkable sentences ("a retried request returns its first result and
  has no further effect");
- the real atomic primitives (one compare-and-swap on one key, a lock, a transaction).
  Everything else can interleave;
- 5-10 concrete scenarios that could break the contract. Always consider:
  two clients that read the same version; a retry after another request changed the
  state (including retries of rejected or empty results); two objects sharing one
  store; each precondition false on its own; values exactly at each boundary.

## 2. Model the algorithm, not the API

- One machine for the store, holding exactly what the real store holds. Its handlers
  are the real primitives: `load` replies with (version, value); `cas` succeeds only at
  the current version.
- Client machines run your algorithm: send load, receive, decide, send cas, retry on
  failure. Every `send`/`receive` is a point where another client can run. If the
  whole operation is one handler, the model assumes the race away.
- A `spec` monitor computes the expected results from the contract and the history of
  requests, independently of the algorithm, and asserts each actual result.
- Drive it with 2-3 clients and small `choose(n)` inputs, plus fixed tests for the
  scenarios from step 1. Start from the [syntax reference](reference/p-patterns.md)
  and [CAS + retries example](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p).

## 3. Check until it passes for real

```sh
snappea check            # every test case, then coverage and mutation checks
```

- Exit 1 is work to do: a bug (fix the design; keep the scenario), a coverage gap
  (add a scenario), or a surviving mutant (an assertion is missing). Read each one.
- Do not finish with `--no-mutation` or `--allow-incomplete-coverage`. Use them only
  while iterating. If search is incomplete, shrink the bounds or raise `--timeout`.
- A bug found here is the payoff: write it down, fix the design, then implement.

## 4. Implement, then test what the model explored

Read [testing the implementation](guides/testing-implementation.md). For each
scenario and each bug the model found, write a Python test that makes it happen on the
real code. Random thread stress rarely hits a race; force it:

- wrap the store so a competing call runs between this call's load and its
  compare-and-swap, or so two calls read the same version before either writes;
- retry a request after another request changed the state, through a second object.

Add an observation test: run real calls, record their actual arguments and results as
events, and check them against your P spec with `snappea.check_events` (install
`pysnappea`, `import snappea`). See [implementation](guides/implementation.md).

## 5. Prove the tests can fail

Break your implementation on purpose, one change at a time (ignore the
compare-and-swap result, drop a retry memo, flip a boundary `<` to `<=`, keep state
in the object instead of the store). Run the tests each time; every break must fail a
test. Add a test for any that pass. Restore the code.

## Done means

- `snappea check` exits 0, with complete search or stated bounds.
- `python -m pytest` passes, including forced-interleaving and observation tests.
- Every hand-made break from step 5 fails a test.
- `DESIGN.md` states the contract, primitives, scenarios, model bounds, what the model
  found, and what is not covered.

## References

- [Syntax and commands](reference/p-patterns.md), [modeling](guides/modeling.md),
  [scenarios and oracles](guides/scenarios-and-oracles.md), [recovery](guides/recovery.md).
- Examples: [CAS + generated retries](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p),
  [reservation + Python tests](examples/reservation/Reservation.p),
  [generated histories](examples/bounded-history/bounded-history.p),
  [durable retry](examples/durable-retry/DurableRetry.p),
  [versioned publication](examples/versioned-publication/Revalidated.p).

Runs test cases over many schedules (event orders, nondeterministic choices) to
find assertion failures, spec violations and liveness bugs. A SOURCE is a .pproj or

Usage: snappea check mutation [SOURCE...] [TEST...] [options]

Runs the test cases, then runs them against mutants: copies of the model with one
small change (a removed statement, a forced `if`, a swapped operator). Lists every
mutant no test case detects: code whose effect no spec or assertion checks. Fix one
by adding an assertion or spec that the change breaks.

Use it to judge whether the specs are strong enough, e.g. as a CI gate. Unlike
`snappea check`, it reports no coverage or scenarios, and fails when a mutant goes
undetected.

Example:
  snappea check mutation tcBank --mutation-timeout 10m

Options:
      --mutation-timeout <DURATION>
                            Time limit for mutation testing (default: 5m)
      --timeout <DURATION>  Time limit per test case for the first run (default: 10s)
  -j, --workers <N>         Worker limit (default: one per CPU core)
      --seed <N>            Seed for reproducible choices
      --latency <FILE>[:<PROFILE>], --timed
                            As for `snappea check`
  -o, --out <DIR>           Output folder (default: PCheckerOutput)
  -v, --verbose             Show progress and statistics

`// snappea-lint: allow mutation[:<kind>] -- reason` before a statement, handler,
function or machine accepts its mutants. See docs/checking-models.md.
Exit status: 0 every mutant detected, 1 a mutant undetected or a test case failed,
2 error.

Output format:
      --format <F>          text or json. Default: text on a terminal or in CI (CI
                            set), else json. SNAPPEA_FORMAT sets the default.
      --json                Same as --format json
      --json-report <FILE>  Also write the JSON result to FILE

cd /work
cat > test_registry.py <<'EOF'
import random
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import pytest

from runtime import Store
from solution import Registry


class HookStore:
    """Real store with hooks: after_load(key) runs after a load returns (outside any
    lock); the hook may call the inner store or other Registries to interleave."""

    def __init__(self, inner, after_load=None, before_cas=None):
        self.inner, self.after_load, self.before_cas = inner, after_load, before_cas

    def load(self, key):
        result = self.inner.load(key)
        if self.after_load:
            self.after_load(key, result)
        return result

    def compare_swap(self, key, version, value):
        if self.before_cas:
            self.before_cas(key, version, value)
        return self.inner.compare_swap(key, version, value)


def once(fn, match):
    """Wrap hook fn so it runs a single time, for the first key/value where match is true."""
    state = {"done": False}

    def hook(key, *rest):
        if not state["done"] and match(key, *rest):
            state["done"] = True
            fn()
    return hook


def is_name(n):
    return lambda key, *rest: key == ("name", n)


def check_consistent(reg, users, names):
    for u in users:
        n = reg.name_of(u)
        if n is not None:
            assert reg.owner(n) == u
    for n in names:
        o = reg.owner(n)
        if o is not None:
            assert reg.name_of(o) == n


# ---- basic contract ----

def test_basic_register_and_lookup():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.owner("bob") is None and r.name_of("u") is None
    assert r.register("u", "Bob") is True
    assert r.name_of("u") == "bob"
    assert r.owner("BOB") == "u" and r.owner("bob") == "u"
    assert r.register("u", "bob") is True          # same name again
    assert r.register("u", "alice") is False       # user already has a name
    assert r.name_of("u") == "bob" and r.owner("alice") is None
    assert r.register("v", "BoB") is False         # name taken, case-insensitively
    assert r.name_of("v") is None and r.owner("bob") == "u"


def test_rename():
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.rename("u", "x") is False             # no name yet
    assert r.name_of("u") is None and r.owner("x") is None
    r.register("u", "a")
    r.register("v", "b")
    assert r.rename("u", "B") is False             # taken
    assert (r.name_of("u"), r.owner("a"), r.owner("b")) == ("a", "u", "v")
    assert r.rename("u", "A") is True              # own name
    assert r.rename("u", "c") is True
    assert r.owner("a") is None and r.owner("c") == "u" and r.name_of("u") == "c"
    assert r.register("w", "a") is True            # old name is free
    assert r.rename("v", "a") is False
    assert r.rename("v", "bad name") is False and r.name_of("v") == "b"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name,valid", [
    ("a", True), ("0", True), ("-", True), ("a" * 16, True), ("A-1" * 5 + "Z", True),
    ("", False), ("a" * 17, False), ("a_b", False), ("a b", False), ("a.b", False),
    ("a\n", False), ("é", False), ("K", False), ("İ", False), (None, False), (5, False),
])
def test_validation_boundaries(name, valid):
    r = Registry(Store())
    assert r.register("u", name) is valid
    if valid:
        assert r.name_of("u") == name.lower()
        assert r.owner(name) == "u"
    else:
        assert r.name_of("u") is None and r.owner(name) is None
    # rename with an invalid target changes nothing
    r.register("v", "keep")
    assert r.rename("v", name) is valid or not valid
    if not valid:
        assert r.name_of("v") == "keep" and r.owner("keep") == "v"


def test_invalid_does_not_free_or_take():
    r = Registry(Store())
    r.register("u", "x")
    assert r.rename("u", "x" * 17) is False
    assert r.name_of("u") == "x" and r.owner("x") == "u"
    assert r.register("w", "") is False and r.owner("") is None


def test_state_lives_in_store_not_object():
    s = Store()
    a, b = Registry(s), Registry(s)
    assert a.register("u", "n") is True
    assert b.owner("n") == "u" and b.name_of("u") == "n"
    assert b.register("v", "n") is False
    assert b.rename("u", "m") is True
    assert a.owner("n") is None and a.owner("m") == "u"
    assert a.register("v", "n") is True


# ---- forced interleavings (scenarios from DESIGN.md) ----

def test_two_users_read_same_free_name_one_wins():
    inner = Store()
    barrier = threading.Barrier(2, timeout=5)
    seen = set()
    lock = threading.Lock()

    def sync(key, result):
        if key == ("name", "n"):
            with lock:
                first = threading.get_ident() not in seen and len(seen) < 2
                seen.add(threading.get_ident())
            if first:
                barrier.wait()

    r = Registry(HookStore(inner, after_load=sync))
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        f1, f2 = ex.submit(r.register, "u1", "n"), ex.submit(r.register, "u2", "n")
        results = sorted([f1.result(timeout=10), f2.result(timeout=10)])
    assert results == [False, True]
    plain = Registry(inner)
    winner = plain.owner("n")
    assert winner in ("u1", "u2")
    assert plain.name_of(winner) == "n"
    loser = "u2" if winner == "u1" else "u1"
    assert plain.name_of(loser) is None


def test_competitor_registers_name_between_load_and_cas():
    inner = Store()
    other = Registry(inner)
    hook = once(lambda: other.register("rival", "n"), is_name("n"))
    r = Registry(HookStore(inner, after_load=hook))
    assert r.register("u", "n") is False           # must re-load, see the rival
    assert r.name_of("u") is None and other.owner("n") == "rival"
    assert other.name_of("rival") == "n"


def test_competitor_takes_rename_target_between_load_and_cas():
    inner = Store()
    other = Registry(inner)
    r = Registry(HookStore(inner, after_load=once(lambda: other.register("rival", "t"), is_name("t"))))
    r.register("u", "old")
    assert r.rename("u", "t") is False
    assert r.name_of("u") == "old" and r.owner("old") == "u"   # nothing changed
    assert r.owner("t") == "rival"


def test_competitor_rename_into_same_target_one_wins():
    inner = Store()
    other = Registry(inner)
    other.register("rival", "r0")
    base = Registry(inner)
    base.register("u", "u0")
    hook = once(lambda: other.rename("rival", "t"), is_name("t"))
    r = Registry(HookStore(inner, after_load=hook))
    assert r.rename("u", "t") is False
    assert base.owner("t") == "rival" and base.name_of("u") == "u0"
    assert base.owner("u0") == "u" and base.owner("r0") is None


def test_name_released_by_rename_is_claimable_and_not_double_owned():
    inner = Store()
    r = Registry(inner)
    r.register("u", "a")
    # v reads "a" as taken, then u renames away; v's earlier answer was False.
    hook = once(lambda: r.rename("u", "b"), is_name("a"))
    v = Registry(HookStore(inner, after_load=hook))
    assert v.register("v", "a") is False
    assert r.owner("a") is None and r.name_of("v") is None
    assert v.register("v", "a") is True
    check_consistent(r, ["u", "v"], ["a", "b"])


def test_swap_cycle_with_both_reading_before_either_writes():
    inner = Store()
    r = Registry(inner)
    r.register("u1", "a")
    r.register("u2", "b")
    barrier = threading.Barrier(2, timeout=5)
    waited = set()
    lock = threading.Lock()

    def sync(key, result):
        if key[0] == "name":
            with lock:
                first = threading.get_ident() not in waited
                waited.add(threading.get_ident())
            if first:
                barrier.wait()

    h = Registry(HookStore(inner, after_load=sync))
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as ex:
        f1, f2 = ex.submit(h.rename, "u1", "b"), ex.submit(h.rename, "u2", "a")
        a, b = f1.result(timeout=10), f2.result(timeout=10)
    assert (a, b) == (False, False)               # each target is held by the other
    assert (r.name_of("u1"), r.name_of("u2")) == ("a", "b")
    assert (r.owner("a"), r.owner("b")) == ("u1", "u2")


def test_rename_to_own_name_after_losing_nothing():
    inner = Store()
    r = Registry(inner)
    r.register("u", "a")
    assert r.rename("u", "a") is True and r.owner("a") == "u"
    assert r.rename("u", "b") and r.rename("u", "a")
    assert r.owner("b") is None and r.owner("a") == "u" and r.name_of("u") == "a"


# ---- thread stress with end-state invariants ----

def test_stress_unique_and_consistent():
    inner = Store()
    users = [f"u{i}" for i in range(8)]
    names = [f"n{i}" for i in range(5)]
    errors = []

    def worker(u, seed):
        rnd = random.Random(seed)
        r = Registry(inner)
        try:
            for _ in range(300):
                n = rnd.choice(names)
                if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                    r.register(u, n)
                else:
                    r.rename(u, n)
                r.owner(rnd.choice(names))
        except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
            errors.append(e)

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(u, i)) for i, u in enumerate(users)]
    [t.start() for t in threads]
    [t.join() for t in threads]
    assert not errors
    r = Registry(inner)

cat > DESIGN.md <<'EOF'
# Unique usernames: design

## Contract
- Names: 1-16 chars of `a-z 0-9 -`, case-insensitive, stored lower case. Non-ASCII
  (including characters that lower-case into ASCII, e.g. KELVIN SIGN) and non-str are invalid.
  Invalid input returns False/None and changes nothing.
- A user holds at most one name; a name has at most one holder.
- `register`: succeeds iff user has no name and the name is free; same name again -> True.
- `rename`: only for a user with a name; to a free name (old name becomes free) or the own name -> True.
- When no call is in progress, `owner(n) == u` iff `name_of(u) == n`.

## Primitives
Only `Store.load(key)` and `Store.compare_swap(key, version, value)` per key are atomic; no cross-key
transaction. Calls for one user never overlap; different users may.

Two kinds of key: `("user", u)` -> name|None and `("name", n)` -> owner|None.
A single call needs two keys, so it cannot be one step: everything between steps interleaves.

## Algorithm (model: `Names.p` `Client`, code: `solution.py`)
- register: load user key; if named, answer `name == current`. Claim name (load name key; if held -> False;
  else CAS None->user, retry on conflict). Then write the user key.
- rename: load user key (no name -> False; same name -> True). Claim the new name, write the user key,
  then release the old name (CAS user->None).
- The name claim is the only contended step and is the linearization point of a success. The user key is
  written only by its user (calls for a user don't overlap), so those CAS never fail in practice.
- Claim-before-release means a user may briefly hold two names (rename) or a claimed name not yet in its
  user record (register); both are "call in progress". It never lets two users hold one name, and a
  crash-free call always ends consistent. Reads: `owner` reads the name key, `name_of` the user key.

## Scenarios (all in the model and in Python tests)
1. Two/three users register the same free name (both read the key before either CAS): exactly one wins.
2. Competitor takes the name between this call's load and CAS: call returns False, state unchanged.
3. Competitor takes a rename target between load and CAS: rename False, old name still held.
4. Swap cycle: u1<->u2 rename into each other's names while both read first: both False, nothing lost.
5. Rename frees a name just after another user saw it taken: first answer False (valid), later register ok.
6. Rename into a name another rename is also targeting.
7. Rename/register with own current name; register with a different name when already named.
8. Boundaries: length 0/1/16/17, case, chars `_ . space \n`, non-ASCII, non-str.
9. Two Registry objects over one Store (state is in the store).

## Model and bounds
`Spec.p` holds the independent `Contract` spec (never reads versions/retries): name claims only when free,
releases only by holder, each reply checked against the user's own history (exact for named users, success
needs a claim, failure needs a rival that held the name), and a quiescent snapshot checked for
bijection and agreement with replies. `Names.p` holds Store/Client/Scenario and tests. 2-3 users, 2 names,
1-3 ops each. Generated test: user0 two ops, user1 one op, op kind and name chosen freely. All 7 tests
complete exhaustively; coverage complete; mutants all detected (19 suppressed with reasons: equivalent or
retry-guards). `snappea check` exits 0.

## What the model found
No race in the final design. Design alternatives rejected while modelling: writing the user record first
(a reader could see name_of(u)=n with owner(n) elsewhere, and failed rename leaves junk), and releasing the
old name before claiming (a failed rename would lose the old name; caught by `test_rename...`/spec snapshot).
Modelling also showed the extra branches "claim finds own name" and "release finds a non-holder" are
unreachable, so they were dropped from the code.

## Tests (`python -m pytest`)
- `test_registry.py`: contract, boundaries, forced interleavings (barrier so both read the same version;
  competitor between load and CAS; swap), second Registry on one store, thread stress with end-state checks.
- `test_observe.py`: real calls recorded as P events (writes in commit order via a store wrapper) and checked
  by `Contract` with `snappea.check_events`; also a deliberately bad history that must be rejected.
- Hand-made breaks (ignore CAS result, steal held name, skip claim/release/set, drop lower/isascii, shift
  length and character-class boundaries, state in object, wrong key, ...) each fail a test.

## Not covered
Crashes between steps (a crash after claim leaves the name reserved by a user with no record, or a rename
leaves both names held); no recovery/GC. Store failures/exceptions, >3 users or >2 names in the model,
